NAYS: -

Finance Committee
Thursday, February 10, 2022
8:30 AMLivestream YouTube

Minutes

Present: Senator Julie A. Rosen - Chair, Senator Bill Ingebrigtsen - Vice Chair, Senator Michelle R. Benson, Senator Bobby
Joe Champion, Senator Mark Johnson, Senator Susan Kent, Senator Mary Kiffmeyer, Senator Melisa Lopez Franzen,
Senator John Marty, Senator Eric R. Pratt

Absent: No Members Absent

Senator Julie A. Rosen called the meeting to order at 8:32 A.M., on February 10, 2022 in Room 1200 of the Minnesota Senate
building.

S.F. 2848: Senator Housley: Promotion of importance and recruitment of peace officers appropriation.

Senator Housley presented SF 2848.

A quorum was noted at 8:34 A.M.

Senator Housley presented the A2 Amendment.

Senator Ingebrightsen moved the A2 Amendment.

Senator Ingebrightsen moved an oral amendment to the A2 Amendment as follows:
Line 1.9: Delete "money" and insert "appropriation".

Senator Ingebrightsen renewed motion. On a voice vote, the motion prevailed and THE ORAL AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDMED WAS.
INCORPORATED AND THE A2 AMENDMENT, AS AMENDED, WAS ADOPTED.

Senator Marty moved the A4 Amendment.

Senator Rosen recessed the committee at 8:37 A.M.

Senator Rosen reconveded the committee at 8:45 A.M.

Senator Ingebrightsen moved an oral amendment to the A4 Amendemnt as follows:
Line 1.4: Delete "2,000,000" and insert "$1,000,000".

Senator Marty requested a roll call vote.

Senator Ingebrightsen withdrew the oral amendment to the A4 Amendment.
Senator Benson moved an oral amendment to the A4 Amendment as follows:
"Page 1, delete Line 2.

Page 1, after Section 1, insert Section 2.

Page 1, Line 4: Delete "2,000,000" and insert "$1,000,000".


Page 1, Line 10: After the period, insert "This is a one time appropriation."
Instruct staff to amend the title accordingly.”

Aroll call vote was requested. The results were as follows:

AYES: Rosen, Ingebrightsen, Benson, Johnson, Kiffmeyer, Pratt

NAYS: Marty, Champion, Kent, Lopez Franzen

ABSENT: -

On a vote of 6 AYES, 4 NAYS, the motion prevailed and THE ORAL AMENDMENT TO THE A4 AMENDMENT WAS INCORPORATED.

Senator Rosen moved the A4 Amendment, as amended. On a voice vote, the motion prevailed and THE A4 AMENDMENT, AS AMENDED, WAS
ADOPTED.

Senator Champion moved the AS Amendment.

Senator Champion moved an oral amendment to the AS Amendment as follows:
"Page 1, Line 2: Delete "delete section 1 and insert:" and insert "After section 1 insert:"
Instruct staff to renumber sections.

Page 1, Line 7: After the period, insert "This is a one time appropriation.”
Aroll call vote was requested. The results were as follows:

AYES: Marty, Champion, Kent, Lopez Franzen

NAYS: Rosen, Ingebrightsen, Benson, Johnson, Kiffmeyer, Pratt

ABSENT: -

On a vote of 4 AYES, 6 NAYS, the motion did not prevail and the oral amendment to the AS Amendment was not incorporated and the AS

Amendment was not adopted.

Senator Ingebrigtsen moved that S.F. 2848, as amended, be recommended to pass. A roll call vote was requested. The results were as
follows:

AYES: Rosen, Ingebrightsen, Benson, Johnson, Kiffmeyer, Pratt
NAYS: Marty, Champion, Kent, Lopez Franzen
ABSENT: -

On a vote of 6 AYES, 4 NAYS, THE MOTION PREVAILED.

The meeting was adjourned at 9:51 A.M.

Labor and Industry Policy Committee
Wednesday, February 23, 2022
8:30 AM, Room 123, Capitol

Minutes

Present: Senator Jason Rarick - Chair, Senator Gene Dornink - Vice Chair,
Senator Michael P. Goggin, Senator Jason Isaacson, Senator Jennifer A. McEwen

Absent: No Members Absent

Committee Chairman, Senator Jason Rarick called the meeting to order at 8:30 a.m. A
quorum was present.

S.F. 295: Senator Draheim: Radon licensing activities regulation transfer to the
commissioner of labor and industry; appropriation.

Senator Rarick moved that S.F. 295, be recommended to pass and re-referred to the State
Government Finance and Policy and Elections Committee.

Testimony From:
1. Nick Erickson, Director of Regulatory Affairs, Housing First Minnesota Senate
2. Dan Huff, Assistant Commissioner, Minnesota Department of Health
3. Charlie Durenberger, Assistant Director, Minnesota Department of Labor and
Industry

Discussion.

Senator Rarick renewed his motion that S.F. 295, be recommended to pass and re-referred
to the State Government Finance and Policy and Elections Committee.

Senator Isaacson requested a roll call vote on S.F. 295. The results were as follows:
AYES: Senator Rarick, Senator Dornink, Senator Goggin
NAYS: Senator McEwen, Senator Isaacson

On a vote of 3 AYES and 2 NAYS, THE MOTION PREVAILED.

S.F. 1547: Senator Jasinski: Department of Labor and Industry study of the adequacy of
benefits for disabled or injured police officers requirement.

Senator Rarick moved that S.F. 1547 be recommended to pass and re-referred to the Jobs
and Economic Growth Finance and Policy Committee.

Senator Pratt presented S.F. 1547 on behalf of bill author Senator Jon Jasinski

Senator Rarick moved the A-1 Amendment. THE MOTION PREVAILED and the A-1
AMENDMENT WAS ADOPTED.

Testimony From:

1. Wendy Wulff, wife of injured bomb squad member Dan Wulff
2. Ethan Landy, General Counsel, Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry

Discussion.

Senator Rarick moved that S.F. 1547, as amended, be recommended to pass and re-
referred to the Jobs and Economic Growth Finance and Policy Committee.



THE MOTION PREVAILED.

S.F. 2698: Senator Cwodzinski: Safety nets installation requirement in certain stadiums.
Senator McEwen moved S.F. 2698 before the committee.

Senator McEwen moved the A-1 Amendment. THE MOTION PREVAILED and the A-1
AMENDMENT WAS ADOPTED.

Senator Cwodzinski presented S.F. 2698.

Testimony From:

1. Doug Johnson

2. Dave Horsman, Vice President of Ballpark Operations for the Minnesota Twins

3. Scott McKown, Assistant Director, Construction Codes and Licensing Division,
Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry

Discussion.

Senator Rarick laid over S.F. 2698, as amended.

The meeting was adjourned at 10:00 a.m.

Minutes
Present: Senator David J. Tomassoni - Chair, Senator Jason Rarick - Vice Chair, Senator Gregory D. Clausen, Senator Michael
P. Goggin, Senator John R. Jasinski, Senator Aric Putnam
Absent: No Members Absent
Senator Jason Rarick, Vice-Chair, called the meeting to order at 1:25 p.m. A quorum was present.
S.F. 3510: Senator Tomassoni: Higher education supplemental appropriations.
The bill title is as follows (see bill):
A bill for an act relating to higher education; providing for supplemental funding for the Oce of Higher
Education, Minnesota State Colleges and Universities, and the University of Minnesota; creating and amending
nancial aid programs; appropriating money; requiring reports; amending Minnesota Statutes 2020, sections
136A.1796; 175.45, subdivision 1; Minnesota Statutes 2021 Supplement, sections 136A.121, subdivision 9;
136A.1241, subdivision 5; 136A.1791, subdivision 5; Laws 2021, First Special Session chapter 2, article 1,
section 2, subdivisions 1, 2, 8, 21, 24, 25, 26, 27, 36; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes,
chapter 136A.
Senator Jasinski moved to amend S.F. 3510 (see delete everything amendment SCS3510A-3, the Higher Education Omnibus Bill).
Hannah Grunewald, Fiscal Analyst with Senate Counsel, outlined the Fiscal Year 2023 appropriations and the ongoing
appropriations in the Omnibus Bill (see spreadsheet).
Joan White, Senate Counsel, explained the higher education policy provisions of the Omnibus Bill (see bill summary).
Testifying on the Higher Education Omnibus Bill were the following:
1) Kate Perushek, Assistant Commissioner - MN Department of Labor and Industry
2) Amy Walstien - MN Business Partnership
3) Pat Benner - AFSCME Council 5, AFL-CIO
4) Commissioner Dennis Olson - MN Oce of Higher Education
Senator Tomassoni moved to amend the delete everything amendment (see document SCS3510A-4).

Minutes

Eric Rudeen – Minnesota Department of Transportation
Senator Omar Fateh
Senator Jennifer A. McEwen moved the A4 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A4 amendment was adopted.

insert “council.” Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the oral amendment to the A16 amendment was adopted. Senator McEwen then renewed her
motion on the A16 amendment, as amended. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A16 amendment, as amended, was adopted.
Senator McEwen moved the A8 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A8 amendment was adopted.
Senator Jim Carlson moved the A15 amendment. Senator Carlson then moved the following oral amendment to the A15 amendment: delete lines 1.28 and
1.29. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the oral amendment to the A15 amendment was adopted. Senator Carlson then renewed his motion on the
A15 amendment, as amended. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A15 amendment, as amended, was adopted.

Ranking Member Senator John R. Jasinski moved A19 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A19 amendment was adopted.
Senator Jasinski moved the A28 amendment. Senator Jasinski requested a rollcall on this motion, and one was granted. The committee voted as follows:
Yes: Dibble, Morrison, Jasinski, Howe, McEwen, Port, Carlson, Hawj
No: -
Absent: Lang, Coleman

-- 1 of 3 --

With eight senators voting “yes” and zero voting “no,” the motion did prevail and the A28 amendment was adopted.
Senator Jasinski moved the A32 amendment. Senator Jasinski moved the following oral amendment: on line 1.3, delete “1,254,683,000” and insert
“1,253,813,000” and line 1.4, delete “1,227,985,000” and insert “1,223,845,000.” Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the oral amendment to the A32
amendment was adopted. Senator Jasinski renewed his motion on the A32 amendment, as amended. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed, and the
amendment was adopted.
Senator Jasinski moved the A18 amendment. This was subsequently withdrawn.
Senator McEwen moved the A7 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A7 amendment was adopted.
Senator Carlson moved the A10 amendment. Senator Carlson then moved the following oral amendment to the A10 amendment: delete line 1.4. On line 1.3,
insert a period after the word “visible.” The A10 was laid on the table.
Vice Chair Morrison recessed the committee at 3:40pm.
Vice Chair Morrison called the committee back from recess at 4:01pm.
The A10 amendment was taken off the table. Both motions were withdrawn by Senator Carlson and the A10 amendment not considered.
Senator Jasinski moved the A42 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A42 amendment was adopted.
Senator Jasinski moved the A24 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion did not prevail and the A24 amendment was not adopted.
Senator Howe moved the A41 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A41 amendment was adopted.
Senator Howe moved the A17 amendment. Senator Howe requested a roll call on the motion and roll call was granted. The committee voted as follows:
Yes: Jasinski, Howe
No: Dibble, Morrison, Carlson, Hawj, McEwen, Port
Absent: Lang, Coleman
With two senators voting “yes” and six voting “no,” the motion did not prevail and the A17 amendment was not adopted.
Senator Jasinski moved the A46 amendment. This was subsequently withdrawn.
Senator McEwen moved the A14 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion did not prevail and the A14 amendment was not adopted.
Senator Jasinski moved the A20 amendment. Senator Jasinski requested a rollcall on this motion, and one was granted. The committee voted as follows:
Yes: Jasinski, Morrison, Carlson, Howe, Lang
No: Dibble, Hawj, McEwen, Port
Absent: Coleman
With ve senators voting “yes” and four voting “no,” the motion prevailed and the A20 amendment was adopted.
Chair Dibble moved the A27 amendment. Via voice vote, motion prevailed and the A27 amendment was adopted.
Chair Dibble moved the A36 amendment. Via voice vote, motion prevailed and the A36 amendment was adopted.
Senator Hawj moved the A43 amendment. This was subsequently withdrawn.

Yes: Jasinski, Howe, Lang
No: Dibble, Morrison, Carlson, Hawj, McEwen, Port
Absent: Coleman
With three senators voting “yes” and six voting “no,” the motion did not prevail and the A35 amendment was not adopted.
Senator Howe moved the A30 amendment. Senator Howe requested a rollcall on this motion, and one was granted. The committee voted as follows:
Yes: Jasinski, Howe, Lang
No: Dibble, Morrison, Carlson, Hawj, McEwen
Absent: Coleman, Port
With three senators voting “yes” and ve voting “no,” the motion did not prevail and the A30 amendment was not adopted.

-- 2 of 3 --

Senator Jasinski moved the following oral amendment: on lines 35.22, 36.5, 36.12, 36.26, 37.5, 38.8, and 39.21, delete “July 1,2024” and inset “July 1,
2025.” Via voice vote, the motion did not prevail, and the oral amendment was not adopted.
Vice Chair Morrison moved the A37 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A37 amendment was adopted.
Senator Howe moved the A33 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion did not prevail and the A33 amendment was not adopted.
Senator Jasinski moved the A26 amendment. Senator Jasinski requested a roll call on the motion and roll call was granted. The committee voted as
follows:
Yes: Jasinski, Howe
No: Dibble, Morrison, Carlson, Hawj, McEwen, Port
Absent: Lang, Coleman
With two senators voting “yes” and six voting “no,” the motion did not prevail and the A26 amendment was not adopted.
Senator Jasinski moved the A47 amendment. Senator Jasinski then moved the following oral amendment to the A47 amendment: on line 1.26, delete
"2024" and insert "2023.” Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the oral amendment to the A47 amendment was adopted. Senator Jasinski then renewed
his motion on the A47 amendment, as amended. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A47 amendment, as amended, was adopted.
Senator Howe moved the A49 amendment. Senator Howe then moved the following oral amendment to the A49 amendment: on line 1.16, after “must”,”
insert “Initiate a trac stop and may.” Senator Howe requested a roll call on the proposed oral amendment. The committee voted as follows:
Yes: Jasinski, Howe
No: Dibble, Morrison, Carlson, Hawj, McEwen, Port
Absent: Lang, Coleman
With two senators voting “yes” and six voting “no,” the motion did not prevail and the A26 amendment was not adopted.
Chair Dibble moved the A38 amendment. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed and the A38 amendment was adopted.
Chair Dibble moved that S.F.3157 pass as amended and be referred to the Tax Committee. Via voice vote, the motion prevailed.
Vice Chair Morrison adjourned the meeting at 5:53pm.
